source_gap_claims.behavior: Network-capable packages must declare allowed schemes and targets, plus named owners for redirects, DNS resolution, private/loopback/metadata blocking, controlled internal exceptions, and timeout.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligation set has no network-specific declaration covering these controls.
source_gap_claims.subject: Network capability declarations

source_gap_claims.behavior: Declaration validation must reject arbitrary URL execution, HTTP downgrade, and missing redirect or address policy.
source_gap_claims.reason: No supplied obligation requires these network-policy failure conditions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Network policy validation

source_gap_claims.behavior: Package A must perform no DNS resolution, URL request, or network-tool installation.
source_gap_claims.reason: The supplied scope and read-only obligations do not explicitly prohibit these network actions.
source_gap_claims.subject: Package A network activity

source_gap_claims.behavior: Inventory mode must report a pre-standard fixture as legacy, strict mode must reject it, and an absent quality sidecar must not silently pass.
source_gap_claims.reason: The exit-code obligation mentions legacy inventory but does not define these mode-specific fixture outcomes.
source_gap_claims.subject: Legacy and strict inventory behavior

source_gap_claims.behavior: A migrated fixture must validate while preserving its owner-specific authority and lifecycle fields, with an oracle comparing before-and-after owner and authorizes fields and failing on drift.
source_gap_claims.reason: Existing protocol coexistence obligations do not require this explicit migration fixture comparison and preservation check.
source_gap_claims.subject: Migration compatibility verification

source_gap_claims.behavior: The reference package must reside under the fixture tree and exercise the published CLI rather than a test-local lookalike.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations require reference-package validation and CLI integration but do not require this fixture-tree and published-CLI identity boundary.
source_gap_claims.subject: Reference package execution identity

source_gap_claims.behavior: Inconsistent policy and schema versions, or an unused policy, must block terminal acceptance.
source_gap_claims.reason: Normative policy/schema use is required, but these specific consistency and usage failure conditions are absent.
source_gap_claims.subject: Policy and schema consistency

source_gap_claims.behavior: A dangling link from the standard to a required reference target must block terminal acceptance.
source_gap_claims.reason: No obligation requires validation of dangling standard links.
source_gap_claims.subject: Standard reference integrity

source_gap_claims.behavior: The reference package must remain a fixture and must not become an installed Skill or a new workflow entry.
source_gap_claims.reason: Existing obligations bound the Markdown standard and governance Skill scope but do not state this reference-package lifecycle boundary.
source_gap_claims.subject: Reference package lifecycle boundary

source_gap_claims.behavior: The repository-owned terminal pytest selection must fail acceptance when a required case is missing, skipped, deselected, xfailed, produces zero cases, or encounters a harness error.
source_gap_claims.reason: Case binding and module inclusion are covered, but these terminal harness outcome rules are not.
source_gap_claims.subject: Terminal pytest completeness and harness outcomes

source_gap_claims.behavior: A negative fixture rejected as expected must count as a passing test and must not make the overall suite fail.
source_gap_claims.reason: The obligations require negative cases and structured assertions but do not define this expected-rejection suite result semantics.
source_gap_claims.subject: Negative fixture terminal semantics
